transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-28
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Ava Thompson (Redwood AE), Diego Marquez (Redwood SE), Rachel Kim (Lumen - Head of ML), Tom Baines (Lumen - Platform), Priya Desai (Lumen - SecOps)

-- Auto-generated Summary (may be rough) --
Ava: quick intro, confirm goals.
Diego: technical scope and bench plan.
Rachel: success criteria and constraints.
Priya/Tom: security and infra constraints.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ava Thompson: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Ava from Redwood, that's Diego our solutions engineer. Quick round-robin?
[00:12] Rachel Kim: Hi, Rachel here. We're excited to scope a POC to replace some of our prompt routing, want to evaluate inference economics and latency.
[00:20] Tom Baines: Tom — I manage the platform side, will handle network/VPC questions.
[00:25] Priya Desai: Priya, SecOps — SOC2 and KMS are must-haves for us.
[00:30] Ava Thompson: Great, main goals for today: agree success criteria, capture workload sizing, outline benchmark plan and timelines, and talk integration options — SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function calling for tools, structured output or JSON schema.
[00:47] Diego Marquez: Quick Q: do you expect to run hosted Redwood API or Dedicated/reserved GPUs for the POC, or do you need Private/VPC right away?
[00:58] Rachel Kim: Ideally hosted to get started, but we have strict data controls on a subset of traffic — might need dedicated or private for that. We'll want to compare both.
[01:10] Priya Desai: To echo, we need encryption at rest with BYOK/KMS and SAML SSO in the later stages, and audit logs.
[01:22] Diego Marquez: Understood — Redwood has hosted, Dedicated and Private options. For the bench we can use hosted first then repro on Dedicated. Note: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation; tradeoff is cost.
[01:40] Rachel Kim: For success criteria, our product goal is: 1) user-facing latency: p95 under 300ms for cached flows, p95 under 800ms for cold calls; 2) throughput target: baseline 200 RPS, burst to 500 for 2-minute windows; 3) quality: responses must meet our internal eval set score (we'll share prompts).
[02:10] Diego Marquez: Good — can you confirm tokens per call?
[02:14] Rachel Kim: On average ~750 tokens, peaks ~1500 tokens.
[02:20] Tom Baines: Concurrency: expect 400 concurrent sessions at peak.
[02:25] Ava Thompson: Noted. On cost we should estimate per-1M tokens for hosted and delta for Dedicated; Diego will run a small cost model.
[02:40] Diego Marquez: For benchmarks we'll measure: p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput sustained for 10-minute windows, and token cost. We'll also test model variants and quantization: 8-bit vs 4-bit where applicable. We'll give you a harness — it's OpenAI-compatible so you can reuse existing integration.
[02:58] Rachel Kim: OpenAI-compatible is important — we have integrations that assume OpenAI endpoints, so that will reduce integration time.
[03:05] Diego Marquez: Right, Redwood exposes OpenAI-compatible endpoints plus native SDKs (node/python/go). We'll include examples for function-calling and structured JSON output (diego note: sometimes product name mis-typed as redwood-serve in docs).
[03:20] Priya Desai: Regarding function-calling / tool calls: we need to ensure any external tool calls can be audited and we can restrict network egress.
[03:28] Tom Baines: Also want deterministic structured output: we use JSON-schema validation in our pipeline. Can the model return consistent JSON?
[03:36] Diego Marquez: Yes — we recommend function-calling for structured outputs, and Redwood has schema-based output enforcement hooks; if function-calling isn't exact we fallback to post-parse validators. We'll share samples of structured JSON responses and the SDK helper that validates.
[03:52] Rachel Kim: Benchmarks — what's your suggested timeline?
[03:56] Ava Thompson: Typical is 2-3 weeks to set up harness and run initial benches, then a 4-6 week POC with integration and iterative tuning. So overall 6-8 weeks from kick-off to POC close.
[04:12] Rachel Kim: That fits our Q4 roadmap if we start first week of November.
[04:18] Diego Marquez: For the harness we'll need: traffic trace (7 days preferred), sample prompts, success eval set, and target SLOs. We can re-run with Dedicated later.
[04:30] Tom Baines: Network: we have egress rules that require IP allowlist and VPC peering. How do Dedicated/Private handle that?
[04:40] Ava Thompson: Dedicated supports customer-managed VPC peering and static egress IPs. Private is available if you need air-gapped or on-prem. We'll put specifics in the security doc.
[04:52] Priya Desai: SOC2 evidence — can you share compliance pack and audit logs retention options?
[04:58] Ava Thompson: Yes — we'll send SOC2 report, compliance pack, and options for extended audit logs retention (add-on).
[05:05] Rachel Kim: For model variants: we may want a heavier model for generative needs and a smaller embedding/parse model for retrieval. Can Redwood route requests to different models based on policy?
[05:15] Diego Marquez: Absolutely — smart routing and model variants supported. You can pin routes and we have fallbacks for capacity. We'll discuss cost/latency tradeoffs.
[05:25] Tom Baines: Bench metrics: can you surface token-level cost and latency per route?
[05:29] Ava Thompson: Redwood Console gives token-level breakdown and per-route dashboards; we'll demo soon.
[05:35] Diego Marquez: About function calling and tools: we recommend designing your tool contracts and providing example schemas. We'll test the end-to-end: model calls tool A, tool returns a structured payload, and then a follow-up parse.
[05:47] Rachel Kim: On dataset privacy — do you retain prompts in hosted mode? How does retention work?
[05:52] Ava Thompson: By default we retain minimal telemetry but you can opt out or configure retention windows; for Dedicated/Private, customer data doesn't enter the shared telemetry. We'll include the data retention policy link.
[06:02] Priya Desai: KMS options? BYOK?
[06:06] Diego Marquez: Yes, Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS/HSM for key control. Hosted has managed keys by default, with BYOK options for enterprise tiers.
[06:16] Rachel Kim: For the benchmark harness, will you provide example code for both OpenAI-compatible endpoints and Redwood native SDK?
[06:22] Diego Marquez: Yes — we'll share node/python examples; the harness is OpenAI-compatible so you can swap endpoints easily.
[06:28] Tom Baines: About stability: if latency spikes or capacity issues occur, can we fallback to a smaller model automatically?
[06:33] Diego Marquez: Yes, Redwood has routing policies for fallback to compatible model variants or lower tier capacity to keep service up.
[06:40] Ava Thompson: Let's capture success criteria again: p95 cached <300ms, p95 cold <800ms, throughput 200RPS baseline, accept quality threshold on eval set. Any objections?
[06:50] Rachel Kim: No objections; we'll send eval set and sample prompts.
[06:55] Priya Desai: Also add a security gating checkpoint before Dedicated migration.
[06:59] Ava Thompson: Agreed. We'll include an item in the plan.
[07:05] Diego Marquez: I'll outline the benchmark steps: 1) ingest sample prompts and trace; 2) run synthetic traffic varying token lengths; 3) test function-calling paths; 4) measure p50/p95/p99 and cost; 5) produce a bench report with recommendation (hosted vs dedicated and quantization).
[07:25] Rachel Kim: Good. Will you also include KV cache behavior tests? Our flows benefit from prefix caching.
[07:30] Diego Marquez: We'll include KV/prefix caching tests and measure latency delta for cached vs cold.
[07:36] Tom Baines: Any blockers from platform side? We need the static IPs for allowlisting.
[07:40] Ava Thompson: We'll provide the static egress IPs for Dedicated hosted tests, and for hosted we can do IP ranges.
[07:47] Rachel Kim: Timeline recap?
[07:50] Ava Thompson: Kick-off first week Nov, harness + run initial bench in 2-3 weeks, then 4-week POC for integration/tuning. So close by end of year if all goes well.
[07:58] Priya Desai: Sounds good. SecOps will review compliance pack asap.
[08:02] Diego Marquez: I'll share the benchmark harness repo (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness) and example SDK snippets.
[08:10] Ava Thompson: I'll share pricing and Dedicated sizing options.
[08:14] Rachel Kim: One more question — do you support function/tool calling with external system adapters? Eg we want to call a ticketing tool via an adapter but no external egress for secrets.
[08:24] Diego Marquez: You can run adapters in your VPC or via secure connectors; function-calls can be proxied to your infra so secrets don't leave your network in Private/Dedicated setups. We'll document patterns.
[08:36] Tom Baines: Ok, thanks.
[08:38] Ava Thompson: Quick recap and next steps: (1) Ava send pricing + security docs; (2) Diego send harness + SDK examples; (3) Rachel/Tom send sample prompts and traffic trace; (4) Priya review compliance pack. We'll set the kick-off for week of Nov 3rd.
[08:57] Rachel Kim: Thanks all.
[09:00] Meeting end.

Notes: transcription contains minor mis-hearings and typos typical of auto-transcript; speaker attributions approximate. References shared: Redwood POC template (https://redwood.com/docs/poc-template), bench harness (github link above), SOC2 pack (will be attached).
